title: A variance proportional to mean wait gives no clear NICER forecast gain in 22 PSR J0537-6910 intervals
abstract: We test forecast spread for the known glitch size-to-next-wait relation in PSR J0537-6910. We fit one affine mean and two Gaussian variance scales to 44 RXTE intervals. In 22 later NICER intervals, the negative log density is 4.5123 for constant variance and 4.7028 for variance proportional to mean wait. The difference is +0.1905 nats per interval. Resampling both series in blocks of two gives a nominal 95 percent range of -0.1876 to +1.0210. Removing intervals that touch small glitches changes the difference to -0.0226. Positive-time and date-range controls retain no clear gain. A simple Brownian first-arrival law motivates proportional variance, but the result does not select a stress model. Missing events, cadence, timing covariance and the small test sample limit inference. No new glitch, source or planet is found. Original code, aggregate results, a figure, exact source hashes and external retrieval steps are included. Raw tables and derivative event records remain outside the baseline bundle.
